name: Kore
overview: Kore was a male Levite serving as the gatekeeper of the eastern gate, a role of significant responsibility in the temple service. He was entrusted with the important duty of apportioning the contributions dedicated to the LORD and the most holy things. His service highlights the faithful stewardship expected of the Levites in maintaining the sanctity of temple worship.
namesAndTitles: The name Kore means 'proclaimer,' which may reflect his role in the temple community. This proper name is recorded in 2 Chronicles 31:14 and was not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Kore was the father of Imnah, establishing a direct familial link within the Levite lineage. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Kore's role as a Levite gatekeeper and overseer of sacred contributions underscores the organized and reverent administration of temple duties during the time of the divided kingdom. His responsibilities ensured that the offerings for the LORD were properly managed, reflecting the seriousness with which temple worship was conducted. Kore's service contributes to the biblical portrayal of faithful Levites who supported the central worship of God in Jerusalem.
